name: Breezy AI Search
author: Breezy Team

sections.description:
Give your visitors answers, not a list of links.

Breezy AI Search replaces WordPress’s keyword search with AI that understands a question asked in plain words and answers it from your own pages, with links to where the answer came from. It only answers from your site’s content.

It works with the search box your theme already has. Connect the plugin, try it, switch it on.

What your visitors get

  • A direct answer to their question, written from your own pages, with the sources shown.
  • Follow-up conversation. They can keep asking, and each answer remembers what they asked before.
  • Search that understands meaning, not just matching words. Typos and different wording still find the right page.
  • Their own language. The search box follows the visitor’s browser language.
  • PDF documents on your site can be searched and answered from too.

What you get

  • Set up in a few minutes. No code to paste, no API keys to copy.
  • See what visitors ask, and which questions your site doesn’t answer yet. A good guide to what to write next.
  • Stay in control. Leave pages out of search, choose which pages come first for a search, and tell the AI how to talk about your brand.
  • Your site stays fast. We read your pages on our servers, not yours. The plugin adds one small script at the end of the page and creates no database tables.

How it works

  1. Install the plugin and click Start free trial. No credit card needed.
  2. Your site address is filled in for you. We read your public pages and prepare your search.
  3. Back in WordPress, open Preview and ask a question.
  4. Choose where search appears in the portal, then open Go live and enable search. Nothing changes on your live site until you do.

Your account, the pages we have read, your analytics and your plan are managed in the Breezy AI Search portal. The plugin links you to the right place.

An account is needed

Breezy AI Search is a hosted service, and this plugin connects your site to it. You need a Breezy AI Search account to use it.

  • Free for 14 days, AI answers included. No credit card needed to start.
  • Then choose a plan that fits the size of your site. Plans and prices: www.breezyplugins.com/ai-search/

“Powered by Breezy Plugins”

The search box shows a small “Powered by Breezy Plugins” line to your visitors. Want search to look entirely like your own feature? White-label, which removes the line, is included in our higher plans.

Good to know

  • Works with WordPress’s own search form, the Search block and most themes. You can also add a floating search button, or open search from any button or link on your site.
  • Search stays off on staging, development and local copies of your site unless you turn it on there, so test visits don’t count in your analytics.
  • Works with page caching plugins. Clear the page cache after you switch search on or off.
  • Works with a strict Content Security Policy: everything travels on one script tag, with no inline script.
  • Part of the Breezy family. If you use the free Breezy plugin, AI Search appears in the same Breezy menu.

Guides and help: www.breezyplugins.com/ai-search/

External services

This plugin connects your site to the Breezy AI Search service, operated by WhooshPro Pte Ltd. It is needed for the plugin to do anything: your pages are read, and visitors’ questions are answered, on our servers.

  • Search widget. When search is switched on, visitors’ browsers load the search widget from ai-search-api.breezyplugins.com. When a visitor searches, their question and the address of the page they are on are sent from their browser so we can answer. The widget keeps a random visitor ID in the browser’s local storage, used only for the anonymous usage statistics you see in the portal. It sets no cookies. The widget also loads on the plugin’s own settings page, so you can try search before switching it on.
  • Reading your pages. Once you connect, our crawler reads the public pages (and PDF documents) of your site to build your search. It reads only what any visitor can see.
  • Connecting. When you click Start free trial or I already have an account, your browser goes to the Breezy AI Search portal (ai-search.breezyplugins.com) and your site address is sent with it, to set up or find your account. The portal sends back the details the plugin needs: your site key, tenant ID and site ID.
  • Ownership check. The plugin adds a small, invisible verification tag to your homepage, and your site’s server asks ai-search-api.breezyplugins.com to check it, sending your site key and site ID. The tag is removed when you disconnect or uninstall.

Nothing is sent until you connect. The plugin does not send your WordPress users, passwords, posts or settings.

Terms of Service: https://www.breezyplugins.com/terms-of-use/
Privacy Policy: https://www.breezyplugins.com/privacy-policy/
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. Open Breezy → AI Search and click Start free trial (or I already have an account).
  3. Follow the steps in the portal, then click Finish in WordPress.
  4. Follow the three steps: Connect, Preview (ask a question), then Go live to enable search.
sections.faq:
Do I need an account?

Yes. Breezy AI Search is a hosted service. Starting the free trial from the plugin creates your account; no credit card is needed.

What does it cost?

It is free for 14 days, AI answers included. After that you choose a plan based on the size of your site. Current plans and prices are at www.breezyplugins.com/ai-search/.

Can visitors ask follow-up questions?

Yes. After an answer, a visitor can ask a follow-up and the conversation carries on: the next answer takes into account what they already asked. Answers still come only from your own pages.

Where do the answers come from?

Only from your own site. We read your public pages and the AI answers from them, showing the pages it used. It does not answer from the wider internet.

Will it slow my site down?

No. Reading your pages and answering questions happen on our servers. On your site, the plugin adds one script, loaded at the end of the page so it doesn’t hold up your content, and nothing is stored in your WordPress database apart from the plugin’s own settings.

Does it replace my theme’s search box?

Only if you choose. Tick “Use Breezy AI Search for my site’s search box” and searching from your existing search box opens Breezy AI Search. Leave it unticked (the default) to keep your theme’s search as it is, and add a floating button or your own button from the portal’s Configuration instead.

I connected, but search doesn’t appear on my site

Two things are needed. Search is off until you enable it: open Breezy → AI Search → Go live, tick the confirmation and click Enable search. And it needs a place to appear: add a floating button or your own button in the portal’s Configuration and publish it, or open Site search box under the steps and tick “Use Breezy AI Search for my site’s search box”. Then clear any page cache. Your theme must call wp_footer(), which nearly all themes do.

Why is search off on my staging site?

WordPress labels each site as Production, Staging, Development or Local. Search stays off on test copies so test visits don’t count in your analytics or use AI answers from your plan. You can turn it on for test copies under Troubleshooting, below the setup steps.

What is the tag added to my homepage?

An invisible breezy-ai-search-verify meta tag that confirms you own the site. It is removed when you disconnect or uninstall.

Can I remove “Powered by Breezy Plugins”?

Yes. White-label is included in our higher plans. See www.breezyplugins.com/ai-search/.

I added the Breezy AI Search code to my site before. Do I need to remove it?

Please do, wherever you added it (for example a header and footer plugin). If both are there, only one is used, so search won’t appear twice, but the plugin’s settings are easier to follow with one copy.

What happens if I deactivate or delete the plugin?

Search stops showing on your site and the verification tag is removed. Deleting the plugin also removes its settings from WordPress. Your account, the pages we have read and your analytics stay in the portal until you close your account there.

Does it work on WordPress multisite?

Yes. Each site in a network is connected, switched on and configured on its own, and each can have its own search. That includes sites that share a domain, such as example.com/one and example.com/two.
sections.changelog:
1.1.0

  • New setup in three steps: Connect, Preview and Go live. Each step shows what to do next, so you can see where you are at a glance.
  • Preview has its own question box with example questions. Try search on your own content before your visitors see it.
  • Go live asks you to confirm before search is switched on for your site.
  • Moved: the header button is now “Manage in portal”. The settings that used to be under Advanced are now under Troubleshooting, below the steps.
  • A setup video in the Installation section.

1.0.2

  • Maintenance release. Updated the search keywords shown on the plugin’s wordpress.org page. No changes to how the plugin works.

1.0.1

  • The magnifier icon on the Try search button now shows on every site, including sites where another plugin restyles WordPress icons.
  • New installs no longer start with “Use Breezy AI Search for my site’s search box” ticked: you choose where search appears. Sites already set up keep their choice.
  • Clearer setup steps: a note under “Switch it on” says where visitors find search, and the “Recommended” label is gone.

1.0.0

  • First release.
